Celsius positioned as the clear leader of the 'next generation' of energy brands; differentiated by seven essential vitamins, six clinical studies, a thermogenic claim, and broad unisex appeal.
Bang's success opened retailers' eyes to a broader, newer consumer wanting more functional beverages; energy is one of the best categories in beverage (6-8% growth, doubling in ~12 years).
CFO confirmed the April rollout is an actual headline (list) price increase, not just a promo reduction; could be rolled back if needed; magnitude withheld.
Average price already rose over the prior year via promo roll-back and elasticity testing, which held up well through ~200% Q1 growth; energy was among the last CPG categories to take price.
Club channel (almost 17% of Q1 revenue, mainly Costco) is fully incremental with no observed cannibalization.
Convenience is the central long-term growth engine; aspiration of ~70% of revenue one day, anchored by the 7-Eleven partnership (Mango Passionfruit launch extended the relationship into 2023).
New convenience doors (5,000 Circle K stores being reset) are far more productive than established-channel stores.
CEO sidestepped the direct Red-Bull-versus-Monster share-sourcing question, redirecting to incrementality (37% of category growth) and new-consumer growth.
Strategic inventory build (excess of 3 months, ~55% finished goods) plus ~97% fill rate; deliberately slowed Asia can transport awaiting price declines and bought US can-manufacturer excess supply.
High confidence of no summer supply disruption while competitors face supply issues; US can prices now moderating; through international cans by end of Q3.
Energy is a daily-routine purchase; higher gas prices could drive more C-store visits (potential tailwind); energy not severely impacted in the prior recession.
E-commerce/Amazon embraced from the beginning by partnering with retailers' platforms rather than building a standalone B2C program; cold/impulse placements drive real velocity.
International framed as a genuine global play (health-and-wellness is global), pursued methodically with the right partners and no over-investment in a single market; ~10% Sweden share.
Vibe-line innovation pipeline (Peach, Tropical, Arctic Vibe) launching this summer, with more Vibe lines to come.
What distinguishes Celsius from other next-generation brands (Alani Nu, ZOA, C4, Ghost, A SHOC)?
Differentiated by fitness/health-and-wellness DNA, seven essential vitamins, great flavor, and a thermogenic claim backed by six clinical studies; 'more than just an energy drink'; #2 on Amazon.
Does Celsius target a different demographic than the other new brands?
Unisex, inclusive brand (50/50 male/female); historically 24-34, broadened younger to 18-24 Gen-Z as distribution expands, while also reaching consumers as old as 67.
Is Celsius sourcing more share from Red Bull than Monster, and what drives the momentum 'ground swell'?

Praised both peers but sidestepped the direct sourcing question; emphasized incrementality (37% of category growth), expanded usage occasions, and the food service opportunity led by EVP Tony Guilfoyle.
What was the magnitude of the April 1 increase and was it a headline increase or a promo reduction?
Tiered three-band rollout fully effective by October; confirmed an actual headline (list) increase, not a promo cut, that could be rolled back; magnitude withheld.
Are you seeing any reduction in promotions from Red Bull?
Broad price-elasticity testing and promo adjustment across the category over 24 months; recently saw a Red Bull buy-two-get-one promo; Celsius confident in its premium pricing.
What percentage of business is in C-stores, and are you seeing a consumer shift to larger formats (Molson Coors flagged C-store weakness)?
Energy is a daily-routine purchase; anecdotal evidence higher gas prices drive more C-store visits (potential tailwind); cited the club channel at ~17% of Q1 revenue, fully incremental.
Red Bull/Monster are ~70% C-stores; where does Celsius's C-store mix stand?
Convenience historically ~25-30% of revenue; 7-Eleven the largest chain; Celsius aspires to ~70% of revenue from convenience one day after building the brand in grocery/mass/drug/club/Amazon first.
Long-term competitive vision vs Red Bull & Monster
How does Celsius think about competing against Red Bull and Monster as the third-largest player?
#4 energy brand (passed Rockstar); growing category leaves room for all; Celsius is a broader beverage play with a Vibe-line innovation pipeline, aiming to be a major beverage-category player.
How did the e-commerce channel develop, why has Celsius done so well, and how does its profitability compare?
E-commerce always core (reached consumers before a distribution network existed); omnichannel approach partnering with retailers' platforms; did not directly address relative channel profitability.
Update on can supply, out-of-stocks and shortages?
Abundance of cans; over three months of inventory (~55% finished); ~97% Q1 fill rate; high confidence of no summer disruption; through international cans by end of Q3 with can prices moderating.
How do you prioritize US vs international investment, and can Celsius be a genuine global brand?

Affirmed a global play; ~10% Sweden share with Nordics room to expand; Amazon in UK/Germany; Asian opportunities (China license, Hong Kong, South Korea, Malaysia, Australia); methodical, profitable-growth, no over-investment in any single market.
